meta.title: HK416 D14.5RS external and terminal ballistics
meta.units: SI: metres, seconds, kilograms, joules, newton-seconds, radians unless a key says otherwise (_deg, _moa, _mm, _hpa, _c)
meta.frame: range tables: x downrange from the muzzle crown, y up, z to the shooter's right. Paths are relative to the line of sight (+ is high). poi_vs_poa distances are measured from socket_ads_eye
meta.muzzle_velocity_note: HK manual value for M855; see ammo.*.source.mv
meta.scope: sport and range simulation: paper, steel plates, earth

source.barrel_length_m: fact: HK manual p.7 (14.5 in); model NOTES.md
source.twist: fact: HK manual p.7, 1 in 7 in right hand
source.sight_height_m: measured from hk416.glb: rear_sight_aperture centre and front_sight_post tip both y=65.5 mm, socket_ads_eye y=65.5 mm
source.eye_to_muzzle_m: measured from hk416.glb (barrel mesh ends z=363.3 mm; socket_muzzle at the flash hider tip z=398.0 mm)

hk100yd.label: HK manual zero: 100 yd on the V notch (drum position 1)

M855.label: M855 ball, 62 gr, steel penetrator (SS109 type)
M855.core: lead with a hardened steel penetrator of about 10 gr (0.65 g) in the nose

source.length_m: recalled: 0.906 in, commonly published for the SS109/M855 bullet
source.bc_g7: recalled: 0.151, Bryan Litz / Applied Ballistics measured G7 (not re-verified today; consistent with G1 0.304 in the check below)
source.bc_g1: published: 0.304 (commonly listed military figure; 0.307 also quoted)
source.mv: fact: HK manual p.7, 2,790 ft/s (850 m/s) for the 14.5 in barrel (ammunition type not stated; taken as M855/SS109 class). Parameter; action/action.json should override it
source.mv_sigma: inferred: about 25 ft/s shot-to-shot standard deviation, typical of service ball
source.group_es10_moa: inferred: 10-shot extreme spread from a service carbine; range reports cluster around 2.5 to 4 MOA
source.sparks_on_steel: inferred probability of a visible spark; steel-core ammunition is widely banned on steel ranges for sparks and plate damage

hk100yd.label: HK manual zero: 100 yd on the V notch (drum position 1)

Mk262.label: Mk 262 Mod 1, 77 gr Sierra MatchKing OTM

source.bc_g7: recalled: 0.190, Litz measured G7 for the 77 gr SMK (not re-verified today)
source.mv: inferred: HK's 850 m/s scaled by the Mk 262 to M855 ratio seen in 14.5 in chronograph reports (about 2,620 against 2,900 ft/s)
source.group_es10_moa: inferred: 10-shot extreme spread from a chrome-lined 14.5 in service barrel; the ammunition alone shoots under 1 MOA from match barrels
source.sparks_on_steel: inferred: copper and lead on steel rarely spark

hk100yd.label: HK manual zero: 100 yd on the V notch (drum position 1)

M856.label: M856 tracer, 63.7 gr
M856.core: lead front core, tracer composition in the base

tracer.source: recalled: specification asks for a visible trace from about 75 yd to at least 875 yd (800 m); red strontium-based composition. ignite_distance_m (dim trace start) and mass loss are inferred. Mass loss and base-burn drag change are not modelled

source.bc_g7: inferred: no trusted published figure; set a little below M855
source.mv: inferred: HK's 850 m/s scaled by the published 20 in velocities of M856 and M855 (about 2,870 against 3,020 ft/s)
source.group_es10_moa: inferred: tracers group worse than ball

hk100yd.label: HK manual zero: 100 yd on the V notch (drum position 1)

dispersion.model: circular bivariate normal in angle; rifle-plus-ammunition and shooter terms add in quadrature
dispersion.es_note: mean extreme spread of an n-shot group divided by the per-axis sigma (Monte Carlo, 40,000 groups, seed 416)

M855.source: inferred: 10-shot extreme spread from a service carbine; range reports cluster around 2.5 to 4 MOA

Mk262.source: inferred: 10-shot extreme spread from a chrome-lined 14.5 in service barrel; the ammunition alone shoots under 1 MOA from match barrels

M856.source: inferred: tracers group worse than ball

aimed_supported.source: inferred upper bound from the US Army grouping standard (5 of 6 shots in a 4 cm circle at 25 m, about 5.5 MOA, prone supported) after removing the rifle's share

aimed.source: inferred: standing unsupported, iron sights, about three times the supported wobble

hip.source: inferred: unsighted fire from the hip, 1 degree per axis. No published standard; tune for feel

dispersion.current_range_page: uniform cone 0.0015 rad aimed (sigma about 1.5 MOA) and 0.025 rad at the hip (sigma about 0.41 degree)

paper.source: inferred: pointed bullets leave a hole smaller than calibre in target paper because the fibres close back (the reason scoring plugs exist); 0.85 is a typical ratio, not a measurement of this target stock

source.momentum_transfer: physics: the bullet shatters and its fragments leave along the plate face, so the plate takes the normal momentum once (coefficient about 1.0, within roughly 10 percent)
source.splash_half_angle_deg: published guidance from steel-target makers: splatter leaves within about 20 degrees of the plate face
source.fragments: inferred: speeds, count, sizes and the drag time constant are visual calibration
source.ricochet: inferred: below about 12 degrees from the plate face the bullet glances mostly intact
source.pit_threshold_mps: published guidance: makers rate AR500 for lead-core rifle impacts below about 2,850 ft/s (870 m/s) and forbid steel-core ammunition; the steel-core threshold and the depth slope are inferred
source.real_world_min_distance_m: published guidance: 100 yd minimum for rifle on steel. The game's 20 to 55 m plates are closer than any real range allows

source.model: Poncelet penetration: depth = m / (2 C rho A_eff) * ln(1 + C rho v^2 / R)
source.density: typical dry compacted soil or sand
source.strength_pa, drag_coefficient, tumble_ar: inferred; chosen so 5.56 mm ball stops in roughly 10 to 15 cm of packed sand, as commonly reported (one sandbag layer stops it)
source.ricochet: inferred from forensic literature ranges: critical angles for soil and sand are a few degrees up to about 10 to 15; exit angle steeper than entry; the bullet tumbles afterwards
source.plume: inferred visual calibration: a 1,500 J strike on dry dirt raises a puff roughly 0.9 m high and a 10 cm scar; scaled with energy^(1/3)

berm.source: inferred: looser, damper banked earth than the trodden ground

steel_notes.hinge: plate hinged along a horizontal axis at its bottom edge (hinge_offset = radius), resting lean_deg toward the shooter against a stop; I = m r^2 / 4 + m s^2
steel_notes.force_pulse: half-sine of duration contact_time_s = bullet length / impact speed, carrying momentum_ns; bandwidth about 1 / contact_time, well above the audible range
steel_notes.energy_split: the plate's swing takes under 0.1 percent of the bullet's energy; the rest goes to breaking and heating the bullet, the splash, and sound

terminal.ground_strike_note: from a 1.6 m eye height the flat ground is struck at atan(1.6 / distance): 4.6 degrees at 20 m, 1.8 degrees at 50 m. Low shots almost always skip off the dirt and carry on into the berm

visibility.source: inferred from shooting practice: 'trace' is the refractive wake of the bullet, seen from behind through a spotting scope or magnified optic in good light, usually past 100 m. To the naked eye over iron sights a ball round is not visible. Condensation in the wake needs air close to saturation and is brief and faint. Values are visual calibration

constant_cd_decay.note: Mach 0.29 where G7 Cd is flat at 0.1194: vx = v0 exp(-k Cd x) to first order in the small fall angle

sierra_infinity_m855.source: Sierra Infinity output for M855 posted on forums.accuratereloading.com (thread 352101342): 3,025 ft/s (TM 43-0001-27), 300 yd zero, 100 F, sea level; BC 0.307 quoted in the thread. Forum transcription, not a primary source
sierra_infinity_m855.fit: a one-parameter refit (G1 0.260 at 100 F, or 0.274 at 15 C) reproduces every posted row within 0.11 in (0.4 in at 15 C), so the posted run did not use 0.307; the integrator and geometry agree with Sierra's, the BC of that run is unknown
sierra_infinity_m855.conditions: sim_g1: 37.8 C, 1013.25 hPa, dry. sim_g1_humid: 37.8 C, 1000 hPa, 78 percent humidity (Army Standard Metro pressure and humidity). sim_g7: this model's M855 drag (G7 0.151) at the same velocity

aberdeen_20in_snippet.source: search-result summary of a forum post citing Aberdeen data for M855 from a 20 in barrel: 2,751 / 2,420 / 2,115 ft/s at 100 / 200 / 300 m. Second hand; the muzzle velocity (assumed 3,100 ft/s) was not stated. Weak evidence

hk_drum_steps.note: bore-angle steps this model needs between HK's drum positions, and what they mean at the rear sight (sight radius 364 mm). HK manual: a quarter turn of the drum is about 1.5 in at 100 yd (0.417 mrad)

hk_ranges.note: HK manual: 500 m point, 600 m area effective range
